5. $229.80–$273.64 — The longer-term downside target zone over approximately 3–5 months. 

Multiple technical support structures converge toward this area by late January 2027, making it the primary bearish objective while major resistance remains intact.

Breaking above it would likely produce an intraday test of $396.10. A move through $396.10 could extend toward $401.45, but this entire zone remains sellable resistance.

The bullish scenario changes dramatically ONLY with a weekly close above $401.45. 

Such a breakout would invalidate the prevailing bearish framework and open the door to $554.20 within approximately six months, potentially by the end of Q1 2027.

But we are far from there.

*

So, Tesla's pre-earnings strength did not eliminate the longer-term bearish setup. The AI CapEx-driven selloff has brought the downside risks back into focus.

Watch $370.50 closely today. Holding it keeps a recovery possible. Losing it on a closing basis exposes $348.36, followed by $306.53 if that support fails.

Until $401.45 is reclaimed on a weekly closing basis, the bigger technical picture remains vulnerable.
